HOLTEC

Subject:       Response to NRC Letter Concerning a Chilled Work Environment for Raising and
               Addressing Safety Concerns at Palisades Nuclear Plant

Reference:     NRC letter to Fadi Diya dated October 13, 2026, EAF-Rlll-2026-0081, Inspection
               Report 05000255/2026010, ADAMS Accession No. ML26286A257.



Dear Mr. Groom:

We are submitting the enclosed Evaluation Plan in response to the referenced NRC letter
regarding a chilled work environment within the Supply Chain and Quality Assurance
departments at Palisades Nuclear Plant.

We fully recognize the significance of the NRC's conclusion that employees within these
departments may be reluctant to raise safety concerns through available avenues due to a
perceived fear of retaliation. A strong safety-conscious work environment and a healthy nuclear
safety culture are fundamental to our mission, our values, and our commitment to nuclear
safety. Any condition that discourages employees from raising concerns is unacceptable and
inconsistent with our expectations.

We are committed to thoroughly evaluating the concerns identified by the NRC, understanding
the organizational and leadership factors that may have contributed to these conditions, and
implementing effective corrective actions that result in sustainable improvement. Our objective
is not only to address the specific concerns identified, but also to strengthen employee
confidence that concerns will be raised, heard, evaluated, and resolved promptly and
appropriately.

The Palisades leadership team and I expect every employee and supplemental worker to raise
safety, regulatory, quality, and compliance concerns without hesitation, including directly to the
NRC if they choose, and without fear of retaliation. We have an equally important responsibility
to foster an environment where questioning attitudes are encouraged, conservative decision-
making is supported, differing views are respected, and concerns are addressed with urgency,
professionalism, and transparency.
 PNP 2026-063
Page 2 of 3


We also recognize that restoring trust requires more than leadership messages, organizational
changes, or corrective action plans. Employees must consistently experience behaviors that
demonstrate openness, accountability, respect, and responsiveness. Recovery will ultimately be
measured by employee confidence in the process and by leadership behaviors that reinforce a
healthy nuclear safety culture every day.

I joined the Holtec Palisades team on July 27, 2026, and immediately initiated actions to
strengthen our nuclear safety culture because it is the right thing to do and essential to our long-
term success, independent of any regulatory inspection or enforcement activity. From the
outset, I prioritized leadership alignment, increased management visibility in the field, direct
engagement with employees, all-hands meetings, and clear communication of expectations to
establish and reinforce the foundation of a strong nuclear safety culture.

Together with the Palisades leadership team, we have continued these efforts and implemented
additional initiatives focused on strengthening accountability, trust, transparency, leadership
effectiveness, and nuclear professionalism throughout the organization. These actions are
contributing to positive cultural improvements across the site; however, we recognize that
sustainable cultural change requires persistent focus, continuous reinforcement, and
demonstrated leadership commitment over time.

While meaningful progress has been made, we acknowledge that much important work remains
ahead of us. Building and sustaining a strong nuclear safety culture is a continuous journey that
demands vigilance, humility, personal accountability, and unwavering leadership attention.
Nuclear safety culture will remain a foundational element of how we conduct business. It must
be evident in every decision we make, every action we take, and every task we perform.

Our commitment is clear and unwavering: safety will remain our overriding priority, and we will
continue taking the actions necessary to ensure every employee and supplemental worker feels
empowered and responsible to raise concerns, challenge assumptions, and contribute to the
safe and successful operation of Palisades Nuclear Plant.

The enclosed plan addresses the five elements requested by the NRC: immediate and short-
term measures; evaluator independence; extent of condition beyond Supply Chain and Quality
Assurance; corrective actions and their effectiveness; and the effectiveness of the Corrective
Action Program (CAP) and Employee Concerns Program (ECP). Attachment 1 incorporates the
supplied Palisades Action List, including accountable owners, schedules, and reported status.
The independent assessment is currently scheduled for December 7-11, 2026.

As requested in the Chilled Work Environment Letter, Palisades is prepared to meet with the
NRC to establish a common understanding of the approach. We will coordinate the meeting
date and the relationship of that discussion to the scheduled assessment with the NRC staff.




Fadi Diya
Senior Vice President and Chief Nuclear Officer
Holtec Palisades

Page 3 of 3

                                  Palisades SCVVE Evaluation Plan


1.0 Purpose and response scope
This plan describes how Palisades will evaluate the environment for raising concerns, determine
why the chilled work environment de·veloped and persisted, and implement and verify corrective
actions. The evaluation will focus on Supply Chain and Quality Assurance while determining
whether similar conditions or causes exist elsewhere at the site or in supporting corporate and
contractor interfaces. The assessment will address employee confidence in all reporting
avenues, including management, CAP, ECP, and the NRC.

The NRC identified opportunities in CAP, ECP, and other information that had not led to
effective resolution of the SCWE challenges. The evaluation will therefore examine both current
conditions and missed opportunities to detect and correct deterioration. It will specifically
address concerns about QA independence, procurement and equipment qualification, work
control and execution, management responsiveness, and perceived retaliation.

2.0 Actions taken and interim assurance
The action plan notes that leadership changes, including appointment of the CNO on July 27,
2026, preceded receipt of the NRC letter. Weekly CNO alignment meetings began August 3,
2026. These actions are identified as context and are not presented as evidence that the chilled
work environment has been resolved. The concern was entered into CAP as CR 26021972, and
the station has been notified.

Additional actions that have been taken are development of a SCWE communications
campaign, and initial short-term measures to reinforce non-retaliation expectations, publicize
reporting avenues, and monitor for indications of retaliation. The communication campaign has
reinforced that a strong safety-conscious work environment is fundamental to nuclear safety and
Palisades culture. Senior leaders conducted 19 all-associate, in-person, meetings with over
500 Holtec Employees and contractors in attendance with opportunities for questions and open
dialogue. Weekly State-of-the-Outage calls have continued since March 31, 2026, which also
provides an avenue to ask questions, and raise concerns.

During the evaluation, the CNO, ECP Manager, and Human Resources will maintain direct
access for personnel who wish to raise concerns. Communications will explain that
management approval is not required before initiating a concern or contacting the NRC. Small-
group and individual discussions will supplement all-associate meetings. ECP will provide
private opportunities to discuss concerns, including for supplemental workers and personnel on
non-day shifts.

Proposed additional interim controls are to extend the weekly ECP observation activity to both
Supply Chain and QA; record observations of management response to concerns; promptly
evaluate allegations of retaliation; and provide a route to an executive outside the implicated
management chain. Human Resources, ECP, and an independent executive will review
proposed adverse personnel actions affecting concern raisers for potential retaliation or chilling
effects before implementation, using existing controls where adequate. The review will include
contractor actions and legitimate actions that could nevertheless be perceived as retaliatory.
 PNP 2026-063
Enclosure
Page 3 of 6

Any urgent safety issue identified through these activities will be routed promptly for plant
evaluation through established processes. Additional teaching and learning discussions will be
scheduled to improve leaders' awareness of how to foster a Safety Conscious Work
Environment in their respective functional areas.

3.0    Independent assessment team
The Independent Assessment Team has been developed and biographies that include work
history, and independence from Palisades have been documented.

The assessment charter will document current and prior relationships with Holtec, Palisades,
Supply Chain, QA, and involved managers; potential financial or other conflicts; and their
disposition. Evaluators will be independent of the affected departments and of decisions under
review. Any conflict will be resolved by replacement, recusal, or another documented control
that preserves the independence of the work. Site personnel may provide coordination and
records but will not control interview selection, participate in confidential employee interviews, or
alter the team's findings.

The team will control its methods, selection of participants, analysis, and conclusions. It will
have direct access to needed records and a reporting route to [executive sponsor outside the
affected chain of command]. It will promptly report emergent safety issues and material
indications of retaliation through protected channels. Management may check factual accuracy,
but the final assessment will retain the team's independent conclusions and identify unresolved
differences.

4.0   Scope methodology and participation
The independent team will approve a written assessment protocol before fieldwork. The protocol
will use confidential individual interviews, focus groups where appropriate, surveys or pulse
data, workplace observations, and document reviews. It will distinguish employees' willingness
to use each reporting avenue from their general willingness to report a concern somewhere. It
will separately evaluate fear of retaliation, management response, confidentiality, feedback,
production pressure, QA independence, and the effectiveness of concern resolution.

All available Supply Chain and QA personnel will be offered a confidential individual interview.
The team will seek participation across non-supervisory staff, supervisors, managers,
employment types, tenure, and shifts. It will document the population, invitations, participation,
declined or unavailable interviews, and any limits on conclusions. Broader site sampling will
include Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Work Management and Planning, Radiation
Protection, Chemistry, Security, Training, Performance Improvement, and relevant corporate
and contractor interfaces. Survey invitations will extend to the site workforce, including
supplemental workers, if a survey is used.

Before fieldwork, the team will establish sampling targets by organization and workforce
category and document why the number and cross-section are sufficient. Low participation,
inconsistent results, evidence of retaliation, or indications of concern outside the initially affected
groups will trigger expanded interviews or additional methods. Sitewide averages will not
substitute for separate Supply Chain and QA conclusions. Small-group results will be managed
to reduce the risk of identifying individuals.

Participants will be told the purpose of the assessment, available private contact methods, the
voluntary nature of participation, and the limits of confidentiality. Supervisors will not select

Enclosure
Page 4 of 6

interviewees or attend interviews with their staff. Interview scheduling and work coverage will
permit access without avoidable disclosure of who raised a concern. The team will provide a
private follow-up route and will evaluate whether fear or nonresponse may bias the results.

5.0   Extent of condition and causal evaluation
The assessment will evaluate whether conditions seen in Supply Chain and QA occur in other
site departments or originate in common corporate, contractor, or management interfaces. It will
examine whether schedule pressure, organizational turnover, uncertainty about escalation
routes, or management behavior has inhibited reporting. The scope will also examine whether
QA personnel can independently identify issues, initiate condition reports, document findings,
and escalate unresolved matters without inappropriate influence.

Palisades will use CR 26021972 to document the results of the independent assessment,
including causes that created and sustained the chilled work environment; leadership behaviors;
adequacy of earlier corrective actions; missed indications in CAP, ECP, surveys, and oversight
forums; reporting barriers; perceived or actual retaliation; staffing and workload; organizational
change; QA independence; and procurement and work-control interfaces.

6.0   Effectiveness of CAP and ECP
The independent team will assess both the design and implementation of CAP and ECP,
including whether their interfaces with management and oversight bodies supported early
recognition of the chilled work environment. A proposed lookback period is August 25, 2025,
through completion of fieldwork, extending earlier where needed to understand causes or prior
actions. This date aligns with site implementation of Technical Specifications, Site Emergency
Plan, and Palisades Security Plan, which resulted in substantial changes to site processes. The
team will document the final period, sample selection, and records reviewed.

CAP review will include SCWE and safety-culture concerns, anonymous reports, repeat
concerns, externally identified issues, concerns withdrawn or not entered, overdue actions, and
prior effectiveness reviews. Sampling will examine low-threshold access, screening and
evaluation quality, escalation, timeliness, closure evidence, recurrence, and feedback to
initiators. The team will determine whether management approval or other informal barriers
inhibited reporting, including independent QA reporting.

ECP review will examine access, independence, staffing and qualifications, confidentiality
practices, investigation quality, timeliness, corrective-action follow-through, trend analysis,
employee feedback, and management response. A risk-based sample will include closed and
open cases, anonymous concerns, repeated concerns, and cases involving alleged retaliation.
Personnel-action records will be reviewed through appropriate protected access to assess
whether concern raising was followed by adverse treatment or whether review controls missed
potential chilling effects.

The team will integrate CAP and ECP information with prior surveys, assessments, employee
forums, turnover and staffing information, and Nuclear Safety Culture Monitoring Panel
(NSCMP) and NSRB records. It will identify what information was available, who received it,
what decisions followed, and why earlier measures did not correct the concern. Findings will be
entered into CAP with appropriate handling of sensitive information. The public response will
describe methods and conclusions without disclosing individual identities or confidential case
details.
 PNP 2026-063
Enclosure
Page 5 of 6

7.0 Corrective actions and oversight
The CNO will sponsor the recovery effort. Regulatory Assurance will maintain the consolidated
action inventory and cross-reference assessment findings, causal conclusions, corrective
actions, owners, dates, deliverables, and effectiveness measures in CAP. The independent
team will provide findings and recommendations; responsible line and program managers will
own implementation. The plan will identify a single accountable recovery manager and an
executive escalation route outside an implicated chain of command.

Corrective actions will be commensurate with the significance and causes of the findings.
January 15, 2026, milestone in the supplied action plan will be used to approve the initial
corrective-action package, implement near-term actions, and establish justified dates for any
longer-term actions. Personnel experiencing immediate safety or retaliation concerns will
receive prompt attention without awaiting the final report.

The NSCMP will review the assessment results, recommendations, and emerging indicators.
Proposed additional oversight consists of monthly recovery reviews during the initial six months
and NSRB review of causal adequacy, implementation, and sustained effectiveness. Actions
that fail an effectiveness review will be reopened or replaced, with escalation to the CNO.
Changes to the plan will retain their technical basis, approval, and traceability to the original
concern.

8.0 Effectiveness measures and sustained recovery
The independent assessment will establish the baseline. February 1, 2027, activities in the
action plan will provide an early independent follow-up and a survey of progress. They will not
by themselves establish sustained recovery. Proposed later reviews at approximately six and
twelve months after corrective-action implementation will evaluate whether improvements
persist. The assessment team will recommend the final acceptance criteria before fieldwork and
the CNO will approve them before implementation results are evaluated.

 Measure                 Proposed review and acceptance basis

Willingness to raise     Trend consistent questions by organization and reporting avenue. Supply
concerns                 Chain and QA must each show improvement from baseline, supported by

Reporting volumes and anonymity will be interpreted with interview and case-quality evidence.
Increased reporting can reflect improved trust, and decreased reporting can reflect either
improvement or reluctance. Neither a low concern count nor the absence of substantiated
retaliation alone demonstrates a healthy SCWE. Employee feedback will be acknowledged, and
the workforce will receive periodic summaries of concerns addressed, actions taken, and
remaining work, while protecting sensitive information .

                                  Palisades Communication Plan


Healthy Safety Culture Communications Campaign

Background

On October 13, 2026, the NRC issued its inspection report regarding its recent review of the
safety-conscious work environment at Palisades, identifying concerns within two departments.
Palisades takes these findings seriously and is taking action to address the concerns and
strengthen its safety-conscious work environment.

Campaign Purpose

Reinforce that a strong safety-conscious work environment is fundamental to nuclear safety and
to how we operate Palisades.

Every associate must feel comfortable raising a nuclear safety, quality, security, or other
concern without fear of retaliation, harassment, intimidation, or discrimination. Every associate
is also expected to speak up when something does not look right, when there is a question or
when something deserves additional attention.

This is a shared responsibility. Leaders at every level are expected to listen, encourage a
questioning attitude, and ensure concerns are evaluated and addressed appropriately. How we
respond when someone raises an issue, matters just as much as encouraging them to raise it.

People come first. Every individual deserves to be treated with dignity and respect.

Key Message

Our standard is clear: Speak up when you have a concern, have a question or believe
something deserves additional attention.

Expectations for everyone:

   •   Stop and speak up when something does not look right.
   •   Raise concerns through the appropriate process.
   •   Document issues through the Condition Reporting (CR) system, including the
       anonymous option.
   •   Contact the Employee Concerns Program (ECP) when appropriate.
   •   Expect concerns to be listened to, evaluated and addressed respectfully.
   •   Maintaining an environment where everyone feels free to raise concerns is essential to
       nuclear safety and to the organization, we expect Palisades to be.
   •   Everyone owns nuclear safety.

Enclosure Attachment 2

Communications and Engagement

Planned Actions

   •   Internal site letter from Fadi Diya reinforcing the importance of a strong Safety-
       Conscious Work Environment.
   •   Weekly TV monitor videos featuring:
       o   Chief Nuclear Officer
       o   Site Vice President
       o   Plant General Manager
       o   ECP Manager
       o   Select Directors (Projects and Regulatory)
   •   Leadership quote slides from CEO, CNO, and others
   •   Audio messaging at site entry points reinforcing the expectation to raise concerns.
   •   Future Town Hall meetings with opportunities for open discussion and questions.
       o   Small group setting to promote open discussion. Approx. 30 people sitting around a
           table.
       o   Subjects: Palisades Excellence Strategy, SCWE, one-page handouts, Q&A
   •   Nuclear Talks focused on safety culture and an Environment for Raising Concerns.
   •   Palisades Excellence Strategy rollout, highlighting Safety as a key focus area.
   •   New Standards Guide content explaining expectations for raising and addressing
       concerns.
   •   New site posters reinforcing the Palisades Excellence Strategy and Safety focus area.
   •   Nuclear Safety Culture Surveys
           •   Continue conducting anonymous nuclear safety culture surveys, encouraging a
               strong participation rate across the site and all departments.
           •   Review and communicate survey results to the site, including strengths,
               opportunities for improvement, and planned corrective actions.


Actions Already Taken or Continuing

   •   All-Hands meetings.
   •   CNO, Site VP and Plant General Manager participation in department meetings,
       including Operations, Security and Procurement.
   •   Nuclear Talks.
   •   ECP, CAP, SCWE information included in New Hire Orientation .
   •   ECP TV slide.

    •   ECP posters displayed around the site.
    •   Continued leadership engagement with employees and department teams.
    •   Open team discussions and additional opportunities for employees to raise questions
        and concerns.
    •   Sitewide communications are coordinated and reviewed by the CNO to reinforce
        consistent messaging and leadership expectations.


Positive Reinforcement

Performance Improvement amplifies its recognition program for "Good Catches" submitted
through the Condition Reporting system during Management Review Committee meetings.

Recognition reinforces that:

   •    Raising concerns is valued.
   •    Early identification of issues strengthens safety and performance.
   •    Employees who speak up are contributing to the success of Palisades.
   •    Leaders are expected to respond constructively and respectfully.


Campaign Outcome

Build and sustain a culture in which employees feel comfortable speaking up, leaders listen and
respond appropriately, and concerns are addressed through established processes - with
dignity, respect, and a questioning attitude.
